_about: The effects the original's script ADDS - entities spawned by name with AddEntity - as each call
adds its one: which .ent, where from the point the call is given, at what depth, turned how and
at what scale. The call site's facts only: what the entity itself is (its sprite, its particle
systems, its light, its own <Scale>) is read from the original's .ent at run time by
Art::LoadEnt and never copied here, since hand copies of the fifty-odd files would drift.
Decoded from android_game.bin through Enhanced's asbc listing (out/parity/asbc/
all_functions.txt, md5 48fe65ce8baea16b94ed84d8d7be84b0). Step 82 of
docs/planning/2026-09-11-magic-portals-remaster.md (the visuals plan's 6.2, system_7 7a-1).
WHAT IS HERE. The rows of vanishEffect and appearEffect (Portal.angelscript), whose
arithmetic test_mp_effects pins: the teleport's three effects, drawn by the visuals plan's
step 7.3. The fireball and its two explosions (7.2). The two entities PortalManager::
insertPortal adds for every portal a shot opens, the burst ETHCallback_portal leaves where
one dies, and that callback's own colours and clocks in placed_portal (7.4). And red_eyes,
MainCharacter's own, drawn by step 7.1 - added once at a level's
start rather than at a call site, so it has a shape and a reader of its own. The shot's
marks and ends (10.1, _shot_side below), what a crystal leaves where it was (10.2,
_crystals below), what a key and its keyhole leave (10.3, _keys below), what a diamond, a
shock ring and a fire signal leave (10.4, _shock_burn_extinguish below), what a wall, a
stone and a lift door leave (11.1, _walls_stones_doors below), and what a torch, its light
wall, a weightless player and a gravity well add (11.2, _torches_trail_roundabout below). And the
level's end and a death (11.3, planning step 96): levelFinishedEffect's red_suck_effect and
red_sparkles, blood where the character or a minion is killed, and skull where either falls. And
chapter 3's ghost (12.2, planning step 98): its shot and the three entities the shot's calls add
(its mark is portal_mark's row, the player's shot's, since the merge of planning step 112), and
the dark puffs that follow it in, with the followUp and Scale their own callback runs. And the smaller
pictures of planning step 146 (_bosses_flames_hands below): the three bosses' scattered explosions and
their deaths' explode, ghost_utility_spawn at every restock, summon and dropped key, the flames addFlames
puts on a burning character or minion, a carranca's dust, and a tapped-away tutorial hand's smoke. Every other
effect the script adds gets its row with the step that draws it, so a
missing row is an effect not yet drawn, not one the script lacks. What reads a row is
sim/Effects, strictly: every field below is required.
UNITS. AddEntity(file, vector3(xy, z), angle, @out, altName, scale), its arguments pushed
last-first (00_order 8.0 rule 3; ETHScriptWrapper.Scene.cpp:131-158). The script's
g_scale.scale(n) is n x screenHeight / 256 (00_order 8.12a), which is n of the port's units,
so offset_units and a z whose `scaled` is true are those n. offset_units is a number along the
call's direction, or - for levelFinishedEffect alone - a pair [x, y] added along none. A z the call writes as a bare
literal is in the engine's own units and does not grow with the screen (00_order 8.12b):
`scaled` false says so; the port, whose unit is one level unit, reads the number as it is.
`scale` is a multiple of g_scale.getScale(), the script's scale for anything it adds at its
own size, which is 1 in the port's units; the entity is drawn at that times its .ent's
<Scale> (Art::Entity::ScaleAt). `angle` is Ethanon's, in degrees, counter-clockwise on the
screen: a number, or the named rule toward_traveller_minus_90, radianToDegree(getAngle(d)) -
90 with d = normalize(traveller - portal) and getAngle(v) = atan2f(v.x, v.y) wrapped into
[0, 2 pi) (GameMath.h:711-715), computed in floats as the script computes it; or
along_flight_minus_90, the same sum on the entity's own direction, which its callback turns it by;
or get_angle_radians_as_degrees, getAngle(d) with d = normalize(enemy - diamond) handed over as it
is, radians where the engine reads degrees (shock_strike alone); or entity_angle, the angle of
the entity the call adds it at, in degrees as the engine keeps it (wall_destroy alone).

WHAT ETHEntity::SetColor DOES TO A PLACED PORTAL, and what the kill fade then multiplies.
PortalManager::update (bytes 138545..139692) recolours its array every frame, AFTER popping any
portal whose systems have been killed (#165-180, #230-246):
#185-188 size > 1: #192-207 portals[0] = PORTAL_RED, #212-227 portals[1] = PORTAL_BLUE.
#248-259 size == 1 and maxPortals == 1: #264-279 portals[0] = PORTAL_RED.
#282-300 size == 1 otherwise: portals[0] = V3_ZERO.
Nothing colours index 2 or beyond, and nothing recolours a portal once it has been popped.
PORTAL_RED (1, 0.3, 0.4) and PORTAL_BLUE (0.3, 0.4, 1) are global initialisers (listing lines
60476 and 60485); V3_ZERO is (0, 0, 0). 00_order section 8.2 (decode D1) cites the same four
call sites while ruling the STATIC portal's own tint out of them.
BLACK IS NOT A BUG. portal.ent's sprite is additive, so colour (0, 0, 0) adds nothing and the
halo simply does not draw: a lone portal on a level that grants two is its spiral and its iris
and nothing else, which is what the original's still shows (out/parity/smoke/nav/01, 1-3) and
what F2 measures as 'no halo tint' until the second portal opens (section 4.4).
ONLY THE SPRITE TAKES IT. SetColor writes m_v4Color (ETHEntity.cpp:493-498), the sprite draws
min(1, ambient + emissive) x m_v4Color (ETHRenderEntity.cpp:112-117), and the particle pass
draws particle.color x ambient alone (ETHParticleManager.cpp:381-389). So the spiral and the
iris are never tinted and never fade with the halo.
THE KILL FADE. ETHCallback_portal #127-142: once its killTime is set, SetColor(GetColor() x 0.9)
EVERY FRAME; #144-158, once GetTime() - killTime passes 400 ms, portal_death and DeleteEntity.
The 0.9 is per rendered frame of a game that ran at the device's rate, so the port applies it
per 1/60 s of frame time (kill_fade_frame_ms): an INFERRED reading that makes a 120 Hz run match
a 60 Hz one, and the only one of these six numbers that is not read straight off an instruction.
killTime is READ BEFORE IT IS WRITTEN (#99-101 against #113-123), so the frame that sets it
neither fades nor counts; both start on the frame after.

beside the arithmetic it belongs to; it is not a number a designer retunes.
